title: candidate mental-model cartography — jonathan reed
recommendation: No hire (hold for senior infra tracks). Recommend extra design-focused loop if leadership wants to stretch candidate.
quick_heuristic_scores: system-design: 3/5 (good patterns but not convincing on scale/cost tradeoffs)
latency-hardware-knowl: 4/5 (clear on NVLink/PCIe but shallow on kernel tradeoffs)
code-quality: 3/5 (quick prototyping but messy edge-case handling)
raw_notes:
Context: Jonathan is coming from a mid-size ML infra team that served internal recommendation models. He was pegged by recruiter as 'runtime engineer with ops empathy.'

What stood out (positive):
- Very concrete incident narratives: described a KV cache corruption incident, the root cause, and the layered mitigations they added (checksum, epoch-based invalidation). Good sense for observability signals.
- Pragmatic latency thinking: prefers micro-optimizations only when they demonstrably reduce p99 by measurable amount; skeptical of premature kernel-level shims without benchmarking.
- Comfortable sketching an end-to-end request path (client -> router -> worker -> cache), annotated where backpressure and head-of-line blocking happens.

Risks / concerns:
- System design answers leaned on single-region assumptions; struggled to describe cross-region replication tradeoffs for KV caches and how to handle inconsistent KV caches with fanout requests.
- When pressed on quantization/throughput tradeoffs, defaulted to vendor docs rather than describing experiments they ran; unclear whether they have hands-on profiling at CUDA/kernel level.
- Security / tenant isolation: when asked about noisy neighbors and memory isolation, suggested cgroup + soft quotas but couldn't outline hard SLO-preserving isolation strategies (e.g., preemptible pools, request admission control).

Behavioral notes:
- Collaborative: often asked interviewers clarifying questions and incorporated feedback mid-solution.
- Framing: started solutions with constraints and success metrics—good habit.
- Communication: concise but occasionally used acronyms without defining them for non-runtime specialists.

Suggested follow-ups if we were inclined to re-loop:
- A focused design loop on multi-tenant cache coherence across regions (30–45 min): push candidate to trade off complexity vs SLO guarantees.
- A profiling exercise: given flamegraphs and kernel timing, ask for interpretation and concrete optimization plan (hands-on).

Hiring decision rationale (my POV):
- Jonathan has strong operational instincts and incident experience that would be valuable for SRE-adjacent runtime work.
- He is weaker on cross-region architecture and low-level model-kernel performance profiling—two areas central to our serving-runtime roadmap for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Given current hiring bar for IC3 runtime (expectation: ownership of cross-region rollout and kernel-level perf debugging), he falls slightly short.

If hiring manager wants a compromise:
- Consider IC2 role focused on observability/incident reduction work on a single region, with a 6-month ramp plan to own profiling and cross-region designs.

RAMP SKETCH (if hired at IC2):
- Month 0–1: pair on incident backlog, own two on-call rotations, get familiarity with our tracing hooks.
- Month 2–3: own a perf project to reduce tail latency for a midweight model; present before/after metrics.
- Month 4–6: design a cross-region cache failover proposal and prototype admission control rules.

Open questions for hiring committee:
- Is there appetite to create an IC2 path that has a well-defined perf-to-IC3 trajectory?
- Are we prepared to fund 1:1 mentoring from a senior runtime engineer for 3 months?

Random artifacts/links I pulled into this note:
- Incident write-up extract (private): GHA-4567
- Relevant PR with flamegraphs: github.com/redwood/infer/pull/1982 (see perf/plots)

Immediate admin: flag candidate as "hold — needs focused loop". If no loop is authorized within 2 weeks, close as "no hire".

Personal impression (tl;dr): strong ops instincts and communication, needs more demonstrated low-level profiling and cross-region thinking to match IC3 runtime bar.
final_comments: Saving this as a user scratch that I can hand off to hiring manager. If we proceed, Evan to own scheduling the re-loop and Aya to craft the profiling exercise.
